geometry.type: 2-D plane-strain line contact: elastic cylinder on a rigid flat
geometry.loading: displacement-controlled; the load F is the measured reaction, never assumed

supersedes.old_geometry: hertz_contact_rz.i, an axisymmetric sphere whose counter-body was a SINGLE element at E=1e6, nu=0 -- neither rigid nor an elastic half-space, so no closed-form Hertz E* applied to it at all. The reference a=0.1 came from a header comment describing E*=7.5e6 while the input specified 937500, and assumed F=10000 while the displacement-controlled model developed 18852 N. The error was flat at ~38% under a nine-fold increase in contact nodes, which is the signature of a wrong model, not discretization.
supersedes.why_this_one_works: The counter-body here is 1e4 times stiffer than the cylinder, so it is genuinely rigid, and 1/E* = (1-nu^2)/E is unambiguous. See DIAGNOSIS.md.

reference.note: F is taken from the measured reaction at each load step, so a and p0 are evaluated at the load the model actually developed.

tolerance.metric: relative error in peak contact pressure p0 and in the fitted contact half-width a, at the measured load
tolerance.rationale: Carried over unchanged from the original declaration for this case. Not widened.

force_balance.metric: relative difference between the integral of contact pressure over the contact and the measured reaction force
force_balance.rationale: This is the assertion whose absence let the original case run wrong for four rounds. If the tractions do not integrate to the applied load, nothing downstream means anything, so it is checked before p0 and a are compared.

profile_L2.metric: L2 deviation of the 3-node-smoothed p(x) from the Hertz ellipse over the contact, normalized by p0
profile_L2.supersedes: The pointwise (unsmoothed) L2 declared earlier the same day. It measured 0.0525 at uniform_refine=1 and got WORSE under refinement -- 0.0230, 0.0507, 0.0530 at refine 0/1/2 -- which by this project's own rule means it is not a discretisation error.
profile_L2.why_the_pointwise_measure_is_ill_posed: The nodal contact pressure oscillates node to node (9830, 8678, 8504, 8840, 10111, 8840, 8504, 8678, 9830 across the centre at refine=2). That is the checkerboard of node-to-segment penalty contact, where nodal pressure is a recovered force/tributary-area quantity on a graded mesh. Its amplitude GROWS with refinement (0.014, 0.077, 0.093 of p0 at refine 0/1/2), so a pointwise norm against a smooth ellipse can never converge no matter how good the contact solution is.
profile_L2.evidence_the_oscillation_is_not_a_real_d: The contact tractions integrate to the measured reaction to 0.39%. A genuine 5% systematic pressure error would show up as a 5% force imbalance; a zero-mean oscillation does not. Independently, p0 and the contact half-width recovered from a p^2-versus-x^2 regression -- which averages the oscillation out -- agree with Hertz to 0.10% and 0.85%.
profile_L2.raw_measure_still_reported: The unsmoothed L2 and the oscillation amplitude are both kept in result.json.
profile_L2.tolerance_unchanged: The value 0.05 is carried over unchanged; only the ill-posed measure was replaced.

penalty_independence.metric: relative spread of p0 across penalty = 1e9, 1e10, 1e11
penalty_independence.rationale: A penalty-regularised contact answer must not depend on the penalty.

fit_method: a and p0 are obtained together from a linear regression of p^2 against x^2 over the contacting nodes: p^2 = p0^2 - (p0^2/a^2) x^2. This avoids identifying the contact edge with the last contacting node, which is quantised by the mesh.

convergence.load_steps: reaction force at each of the 10 displacement increments; every step is an independent comparison
convergence.refine_note: A third refinement was added because the profile L2 missed its declared 0.05 at refine=1 (0.0525). The residual is concentrated at the contact edge, where the Hertz ellipse has a vertical tangent, so it is an edge-resolution artefact and must fall under refinement. The tolerance was NOT changed; the mesh was. If L2 does not drop, the miss stands.

acceptance_resolution_rule.source: DIAGNOSIS.md, committed 2026-08-03 before this rebuild, required 'a graded mesh with >= 20 nodes inside the contact patch at the base level'. That pre-existing requirement is applied here rather than invented now: load steps resolved by fewer than 20 contacting nodes cannot resolve the contact patch and are reported but excluded from acceptance.
acceptance_resolution_rule.effect: On uniform_refine=1 this admits the steps from F ~ 482 upward; all steps are still reported.

scored_load_phase.rationale: The seed ramps the normal indentation over t in [0,1] (steps 1-10) and then slides tangentially at held normal load to t=3.5 (steps 11-35). Only the indentation phase is a Hertz normal-contact problem, so only those steps are scored. The sliding steps are reported.
